findings.claim: diagrams-stay-current requires a `depicts:` front-matter field on every diagram, but OKF v0.2 does not define it and no ADR names it; ADR 0009 says any extension field other than handoff_key needs its own ADR, and okf-bundle.md restates that kmctl uses only spec fields plus ADR-named ones.

measure-before-ticketing says a measurement spike is `loopctl plan spike` with its scripts kept in the spike (under .loop/), while docs-layout says a spike goes to .okf/ and that every script producing a number lives in .okf/prototypes/<name>/. The two kept rules give different homes for the same measurement.

verdict.text: The change does what the plan asks.
The three rules about loopctl's internals are gone, the kept rules cite only ADRs 0001 to 0009 and paths that exist or are planned, no aim-managed rule changed, and AGENTS.md drops the ticket note.
Gates are green.
Two kept rules make claims that do not quite square with the design or with each other; both are plain text fixes, so the label is fix.
`loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree: lint, format, tests and eval rows r1 to r4 all pass; "stamp green: 0d6ad503e10271cc0097f4b31d672eff651bf1d0d8fd76da19c8c98ada819b69".
Rows r1 to r4: read tests/test_rules.py.

In a scratch copy I appended "loop-harness v2", "ADR 0039", a backticked `.okf/architecture/cli-and-plugin.md` and `src/loop_harness/x.py` to okf-bundle.md and the slug to AGENTS.md; r1, r2, r3 and r4 each failed on the planted defect.
The tests assert the rows' fails_when.
